To the Appeals Review Department:

I am writing to formally appeal the denial of prior authorization for total ankle replacement (CPT 27702), as communicated in the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-25 (Reference No. POC-3E3F8049CD-32778). The stated reason for denial was that "the documentation submitted was incomplete and does not allow a determination of medical necessity." I am submitting this appeal, together with supplemental clinical information, to address that stated gap and to request that the plan identify precisely which element(s) of its medical policy remain unaddressed so they can be resolved.

1. Applicable Medical Policy

I understand that BlueCross BlueShield of South Carolina applies its medical policy titled "Total Ankle Replacement," policy number CAM 70177, available at:
https://www.medicalpolicy.southcarolinablues.com/web/public/brands/medicalpolicy/external-policies/total-ankle-replacement/

I was unable to independently confirm a specific "effective date" printed on the policy itself. The most recent confirmed review reference I could locate is BlueCross BlueShield of South Carolina's January 2026 Medical Policy Updates bulletin, which states: "CAM 70177 Total Ankle Replacement (Annual review, no change to policy intent.)" I ask that the plan confirm, in writing, the exact version and date of CAM 70177 that was applied to my request, as required for a complete and reviewable determination.

2. Medical-Necessity Criteria and How My Records Address Them

The policy states:

"Total ankle replacement using an FDA approved device may be considered MEDICALLY NECESSARY in skeletally mature patients with moderate to severe ankle (tibiotalar) pain that limits daily activity and who have the following conditions: Arthritis in adjacent joints (i.e., subtalar or midfoot); OR Severe arthritis of the contralateral ankle; OR Arthrodesis of the contralateral ankle; OR Inflammatory (e.g., rheumatoid) arthritis"

Regarding the "moderate to severe ankle (tibiotalar) pain that limits daily activity" element, my record includes:
- 14 months of progressive ankle pain unrelieved by rest;
- Weight-bearing ankle radiographs (2026-06-18) showing tibiotalar joint space obliteration with subchondral cysts;
- An antalgic gait with ambulation limited to two blocks;
- Positive provocative testing on the affected side and range of motion limited by pain;
- Failure of conservative management, including 4 months of NSAIDs with inadequate relief, and a corticosteroid injection (2026-05-19) that provided only 3 weeks of partial relief.

Regarding the second, disjunctive part of the criterion (arthritis in adjacent joints; severe arthritis of the contralateral ankle; arthrodesis of the contralateral ankle; or inflammatory arthritis), the clinical summary available to me does not contain documentation specifically addressing this element. I am requesting that Dr. Okafor's office supplement the file with [imaging, exam findings, or diagnosis documentation establishing subtalar/midfoot joint arthritis, contralateral ankle arthritis or prior arthrodesis, or an inflammatory arthritis diagnosis, whichever applies], and I ask the plan to confirm that this is in fact the specific element it found missing, since the denial notice did not identify which portion of the documentation was incomplete.

Regarding the policy's contraindication criteria, the policy states:

"Absolute contraindications to ankle arthroplasty include any of the following: Extensive avascular necrosis of the talar dome; Compromised bone stock or soft tissue (including skin and muscle); Severe malalignment (e.g., > 15 degrees) not correctable by surgery; Active ankle joint infection; Peripheral vascular disease; Charcot neuroarthropathy."

My record documents no active infection. I am asking Dr. Okafor to confirm and document the absence of the remaining absolute contraindications (avascular necrosis of the talar dome, compromised bone stock or soft tissue, severe malalignment greater than 15 degrees, peripheral vascular disease, and Charcot neuroarthropathy), as this was not itemized in the clinical summary provided to me.

The policy further states, under Policy Guidelines:

"Patients should have no functional barriers to participation in a rehabilitation program."

My record documents completion of 16 weeks (24 visits) of supervised physical therapy focused on ankle strengthening and balance (2026-03-13 to 2026-07-03), demonstrating both my ability to participate in, and my exhaustion of, a structured rehabilitation program prior to requesting surgery.

3. Additional Relevant Facts

- No untreated substance use is documented.
- BMI is 29.
- Patient is a non-smoker.
- Surgeon: Dr. Okafor, MD, Orthopedic Surgery.

I recognize that the policy's "Policy Guidelines" section also references patient age (">50") and body habitus ("thin") as descriptive of "optimal candidates," not as independent coverage requirements listed in the Policy statement itself. [Patient's age] is not included in the clinical summary provided to me; I ask that this be considered together with the rest of the file to the extent the plan deems it relevant.

4. Requested Action

I respectfully request that BlueCross BlueShield of South Carolina:
1. Identify, in writing, the specific element(s) of CAM 70177 that the original submission failed to address;
2. Consider the supplemental documentation described above once received from Dr. Okafor's office; and
3. Reverse the denial and approve prior authorization for CPT 27702 (total ankle replacement) upon confirmation that the applicable medical-necessity criteria have been met.

5. Enclosures

- Physical therapy discharge note (2026-03-13 to 2026-07-03, 24 visits)
- Medication/injection records (NSAID trial; corticosteroid injection dated 2026-05-19)
- Weight-bearing ankle radiograph report dated 2026-06-18
- Clinic notes documenting gait, ambulation distance, and provocative testing
- [Any additional records supplied by Dr. Okafor addressing adjacent-joint/contralateral ankle/inflammatory arthritis status and contraindication findings]
- [Designation of Authorized Representative to Appeal form, if this appeal is being filed by someone other than the member]

I am submitting this appeal in writing within the 180-day period stated in the denial notice, with a deadline of 2027-02-21. Please direct any questions or requests for additional information to me at [phone number] or [email address], or to Dr. Okafor's office at [surgeon's office phone/fax].

Thank you for your prompt attention to this appeal.

Sincerely,

_____________________________
Riley Lawson
